description.en: Why many models beat one: when voting helps, how stacking, bagging, random forests and AdaBoost build their members, why averaging cuts variance, and where AdaBoost's weights come from.

title.en: Many models, one answer
title.zh: 很多模型，一个答案

text.en: Until now we compared classifiers and picked the best one. But each test instance gets **one shot** at one model, with all the bias of that algorithm. **Ensemble learning** (classifier combination) trains a set of base classifiers and aggregates their outputs into a single meta-classifier.
text.zh: 到目前为止，我们都是比较几个分类器、挑最好的那个。可每个测试实例只能由一个模型判一次，带着这个算法全部的偏差。**集成学习**（ensemble learning，也叫分类器组合）训练一组基分类器，把它们的输出汇总成一个元分类器。

text.en: The simplest aggregation is **voting**. For classification choose the class most base classifiers predict (majority vote); for regression take the average, for example the predictions $0.8, 0.7, 0.2, 0.9$ give $\frac{0.8+0.7+0.2+0.9}{4} = 0.65$.
text.zh: 最简单的汇总是**投票**（voting）。分类时选多数基分类器预测的类别（多数投票）；回归时取平均，例如预测 $0.8, 0.7, 0.2, 0.9$ 得 $\frac{0.8+0.7+0.2+0.9}{4} = 0.65$。

text.en: The two intuitions
text.zh: 两条直觉

items.en: **Intuition 1.** A combination of many **weak** classifiers can be at least as good as one strong classifier.
items.zh: **直觉 1。** 许多**弱**分类器的组合，可以至少和一个强分类器一样好。

items.en: **Intuition 2.** A combination of several **strong** classifiers is (usually) at least as good as the best of them.
items.zh: **直觉 2。** 几个**强**分类器的组合，（通常）至少和其中最好的一个一样好。

title.en: When does voting work?
title.zh: 投票什么时候有用？

text.en: Three classifiers vote on three test instances; ✓ means right. Which scenario helps?
text.zh: 三个分类器对三个测试实例投票；✓ 表示判对。哪种情形有帮助？

text.en: Scenario A
text.zh: 情形 A

text.en: Scenario B
text.zh: 情形 B

text.en: Scenario C
text.zh: 情形 C

items.en: **A.** Each classifier is wrong on a different instance. The vote is right on all three: **the errors cancel.**
items.zh: **A。** 每个分类器错在不同的实例上。投票三个全对：**错误互相抵消。**

items.en: **B.** All three make the same mistake, so the vote repeats it: **no gain.**
items.zh: **B。** 三个犯同样的错，投票只是把错误重复一遍：**没有收益。**

items.en: **C.** Each classifier is right on only 1 of 3 (accuracy $\frac13$, worse than chance for two classes). The majority is wrong everywhere: **voting amplifies bad classifiers.**
items.zh: **C。** 每个分类器只对 3 个里的 1 个（准确率 $\frac13$，比二分类的随机猜测还差）。多数票处处出错：**投票会放大糟糕的分类器。**

title.en: Two conditions
title.zh: 两个条件

body.en: An ensemble works when (1) the classifiers **do not make the same mistakes** (different biases) and (2) each is **reasonably accurate**, better than chance (error below 0.5).
body.zh: 集成有效需要：(1) 分类器**不犯同样的错**（偏差不同）；(2) 每个都**相当准确**，好于随机（错误率低于 0.5）。

prompt.en: Five classifiers are trained on exactly the same data with the same algorithm and the same settings. What does a majority vote give?
prompt.zh: 五个分类器用同样的数据、同样的算法、同样的设置训练。多数投票会得到什么？

label.en: Better than any single one, because five votes are more reliable than one
label.zh: 比任何一个都好，因为五票比一票可靠

feedback.en: They are identical, so the five votes are one vote counted five times: scenario B.
feedback.zh: 它们完全一样，五票其实是同一票数了五遍：这就是情形 B。

label.en: Exactly the same as one of them
label.zh: 和其中任何一个完全相同

label.en: Worse, because the votes cancel
label.zh: 更差，因为票互相抵消

feedback.en: Identical votes do not cancel: they all agree, so the majority is the single model's answer.
feedback.zh: 相同的票不会抵消：它们完全一致，多数票就是单个模型的答案。

explain.en: Diversity is what voting needs. That is why every ensemble method below is a recipe for making the members **different**.
explain.zh: 投票需要的是差异。所以下面每一种集成方法，都是在教你怎么把成员做得**不一样**。

title.en: How much does an ensemble help? A binomial calculation
title.zh: 集成能帮多少？一个二项分布的计算

say.en: Let $K$ be the number of wrong members and $P_E$ the ensemble error. With a majority vote of an odd number $n$ of members, the ensemble errs exactly when more than half of them err.
say.zh: 设 $K$ 为判错的成员数，$P_E$ 为集成的错误率。奇数 $n$ 个成员做多数投票，当且仅当超过一半成员判错时，集成才判错。

say.en: Three members, each wrong with probability $\epsilon$, **independently**. Ensemble wrong = exactly 2 wrong (choose which 2: $\binom32 = 3$ ways, both wrong, the third right) or all 3 wrong.
say.zh: 三个成员，各自以概率 $\epsilon$ 出错，且**相互独立**。集成出错 = 恰好 2 个错（选哪 2 个：$\binom32 = 3$ 种，两个错、第三个对）或 3 个全错。

say.en: Three members of error 0.3 combine to error 0.216. Better than any member.
say.zh: 三个错误率 0.3 的成员，组合后错误率是 0.216，比任何一个成员都低。

say.en: In general the number of wrong members is binomial: the probability of exactly $i$ wrong is $\binom ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{n-i}$ (a sum of $n$ independent yes/no trials). Add up all $i$ above $n/2$.
say.zh: 一般地，判错的成员数服从二项分布：恰好 $i$ 个错的概率是 $\binom ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{n-i}$（$n$ 次独立的“是/否”试验之和）。把所有大于 $n/2$ 的 $i$ 加起来。

say.en: The lecture's example: 25 independent classifiers with error 0.35 vote. Wrong needs at least 13 of them wrong. The ensemble error drops from 0.35 to about **0.06**.
say.zh: 课上的例子：25 个独立的、错误率 0.35 的分类器投票。判错需要至少 13 个出错。集成错误率从 0.35 降到约 **0.06**。

say.en: The same formula with members worse than chance: the ensemble gets **worse** (0.55 becomes 0.69). At $\epsilon = 0.5$ it stays 0.5.
say.zh: 同一个公式，成员比随机还差：集成**更差**（0.55 变成 0.69）。$\epsilon = 0.5$ 时仍是 0.5。

intro.en: Assume (generously) that the $n$ base classifiers err **independently**, each with probability $\epsilon$. How often does the majority vote err?
intro.zh: （很慷慨地）假设 $n$ 个基分类器**相互独立**地出错，每个的错误概率都是 $\epsilon$。多数投票多久会出错一次？

outro.en: This is the arithmetic behind Intuition 1: many weak classifiers with $\epsilon < 0.5$ make a strong one. The catch is the word *independently*.
outro.zh: 这就是直觉 1 背后的算术：许多 $\epsilon < 0.5$ 的弱分类器能组成一个强分类器。关键是“相互独立”这个词。

title.en: The error curve, and the catch
title.zh: 错误率曲线，与它的陷阱

alt.en: Ensemble error against base classifier error for 25 members. The independent curve is S-shaped, below the diagonal when the base error is under 0.5 and above it when over 0.5; identical classifiers lie on the diagonal. The point 0.35 maps to 0.06.
alt.zh: 25 个成员的集成错误率对单个分类器错误率的曲线。相互独立时曲线呈 S 形：单个错误率低于 0.5 时在对角线下面，高于 0.5 时在上面；完全相同的分类器落在对角线上。0.35 对应 0.06。

items.en: **Below 0.5** the ensemble beats its members, and more members help more. **Above 0.5** it is worse: \"better than chance\" is a real condition.
items.zh: **低于 0.5**：集成优于成员，成员越多越有利。**高于 0.5**：集成更差：“好于随机”是个实在的条件。

items.en: The orange curve assumes independence, which is **usually false**: members trained on the same data make correlated errors. The blue diagonal is the other extreme, identical members. Real ensembles sit between the two, and the whole art is pushing them toward the orange curve. How correlation limits the gain is derived below.
items.zh: 橙色曲线假设了独立性，而这**通常不成立**：用同一份数据训练的成员，错误是相关的。蓝色对角线是另一个极端，成员完全相同。真实的集成落在两者之间，全部技巧就是把它往橙色曲线那边推。相关性怎样限制收益，下面会推出来。

prompt.en: Five classifiers each have error 0.3 but always make the **same** mistakes. What is the error of their majority vote?
prompt.zh: 五个分类器错误率都是 0.3，但总是犯**同样**的错。它们多数投票的错误率是多少？

label.en: $0.163$, as the binomial formula says for $n = 5$

feedback.en: The binomial formula needs independent errors. Here they are perfectly correlated.
feedback.zh: 二项公式要求错误独立。这里它们完全相关。

feedback.en: The vote is wrong exactly when the shared mistake happens, i.e. on 30% of instances, not 70%.
feedback.zh: 只在那个共同的错误出现时投票才错，也就是 30% 的实例，不是 70%。

label.en: $0.3$: no better than one of them
label.zh: $0.3$：不比其中一个更好

explain.en: Perfectly correlated members are one member. The diagonal of the figure.
explain.zh: 完全相关的成员就是一个成员，对应图里的对角线。

title.en: Stacking: learn how to combine
title.zh: 堆叠：学会怎么组合

text.en: Voting treats every member alike. **Stacking** (stacked generalisation) instead *learns* how much to trust each one. The intuition: smooth out the errors over algorithms with different biases.
text.zh: 投票对每个成员一视同仁。**堆叠**（stacking，stacked generalisation）则是*学出来*该多信任每一个成员。直觉：把不同偏差的算法的错误互相抹平。

items.en: **Level 0:** train different base classifiers on the training data $(X, y)$, for example a neural network, Naive Bayes and a decision tree.
items.zh: **第 0 层：** 在训练数据 $(X, y)$ 上训练不同的基分类器，如神经网络、朴素贝叶斯、决策树。

items.en: **New data:** for each instance form $X_{new} = [\hat y_{C_1}, \hat y_{C_2}, \hat y_{C_3}, \dots, X_{old}]$: the predictions, optionally their confidences (e.g. NB probabilities), and optionally the original features (keep or discard $X$).
items.zh: **新数据：** 对每个实例构造 $X_{new} = [\hat y_{C_1}, \hat y_{C_2}, \hat y_{C_3}, \dots, X_{old}]$：各分类器的预测，可选地加上它们的置信度（如 NB 的概率），也可选地保留原特征（保留或丢弃 $X$）。

items.en: **Level 1:** train a **meta-classifier** on $X_{new}$ to predict $y$. Typically logistic regression. Its weights are how much it trusts each base classifier.
items.zh: **第 1 层：** 在 $X_{new}$ 上训练一个**元分类器**（meta-classifier）去预测 $y$，通常是逻辑回归。它的权重就是对每个基分类器的信任程度。

rows.en: mathematically simple; combines **heterogeneous** classifiers of varying quality
rows.zh: 数学上简单；能组合**不同类型**、水平不一的分类器

rows.en: computationally expensive: many models plus a meta-model, with cross-validation
rows.zh: 计算昂贵：许多模型加一个元模型，还要交叉验证

rows.en: generally as good as, or better than, the best base classifier
rows.zh: 通常不比最好的基分类器差，甚至更好

rows.en: less interest in theory (statistical learning); mostly seen in applied work
rows.zh: 理论上关注较少（统计学习），多见于应用研究

title.en: Building the meta-classifier's training data without cheating
title.zh: 怎样不作弊地造出元分类器的训练数据

text.en: A trap: the meta-classifier must learn from predictions the base models make on data they have **not seen**. If a decision tree grown to full depth predicts its own training instances, it is right every time, and the meta-classifier will learn \"always trust the tree\". At test time the tree is not perfect, and the stacked model is miscalibrated. So the question in the lecture is: how do we make sure none of the level-0 classifiers sees the level-1 test data?
text.zh: 一个陷阱：元分类器必须从基模型在**没见过的数据**上做出的预测里学习。如果一棵长满的决策树去预测它自己的训练实例，它每次都对，元分类器就会学成“永远相信这棵树”。到测试时，这棵树并不完美，堆叠的模型就失准了。所以课上的问题是：怎么保证没有一个第 0 层分类器见过第 1 层的测试数据？

alt.en: Three rows of three blocks: in each row two blue blocks are used for training the level-0 model and one orange block is held out. The held-out predictions of the three rows are collected into one table of out-of-fold predictions, the training data of the level-1 meta-classifier.
alt.zh: 三行、每行三块：每行两块蓝色用来训练第 0 层模型，一块橙色留出。三行留出部分的预测汇集成一张折外预测表，作为第 1 层元分类器的训练数据。

items.en: Split the training data into $K$ folds. For each fold, train every level-0 model on the other $K-1$ folds and predict the held-out fold.
items.zh: 把训练数据分成 $K$ 折。对每一折，用其余 $K-1$ 折训练每个第 0 层模型，再预测这一折。

items.en: Stack the held-out predictions. Every training instance now has **out-of-fold** predictions, made by models that never saw it. This is the level-1 training set.
items.zh: 把留出折上的预测叠起来。每个训练实例现在都有**折外**（out-of-fold）预测，由从没见过它的模型做出。这就是第 1 层的训练集。

items.en: Train the meta-classifier on it. At test time use level-0 models retrained on all the data.
items.zh: 在它上面训练元分类器。测试时用在全部数据上重训的第 0 层模型。

text.en: The lecture draws this as **nested cross-validation**: the internal (level-0) models are never exposed to the level-1 test split, they still get enough data to train, and every instance can serve as level-1 test data, so all the data is used to evaluate the meta-classifier.
text.zh: 课上把它画成**嵌套交叉验证**：内层（第 0 层）模型从不接触第 1 层的测试折，却仍有足够数据可训练，并且每个实例都能当第 1 层的测试数据，所以全部数据都用来评估元分类器。

prompt.en: The meta-classifier is trained on predictions that the base models made on their own training data. What goes wrong?
prompt.zh: 元分类器用的是基模型对自己训练数据做出的预测。会出什么问题？

label.en: Nothing: more data is always better
label.zh: 没问题：数据越多越好

feedback.en: The predictions are not more data, they are biased data: an overfit model looks perfect on what it has seen.
feedback.zh: 这些预测不是更多数据，而是有偏的数据：过拟合的模型对见过的数据看起来完美。

label.en: The meta-classifier cannot be trained because the labels are missing
label.zh: 元分类器没法训练，因为缺标签

feedback.en: The labels $y$ are there. The problem is how reliable the base predictions are.
feedback.zh: 标签 $y$ 是有的。问题在于基模型预测有多可靠。

label.en: It over-trusts the base models that overfit most, and test performance disappoints
label.zh: 它会过度信任过拟合最严重的基模型，测试表现令人失望

explain.en: Out-of-fold predictions imitate what the base models will do on genuinely new data, which is what the meta-classifier has to be trained for.
explain.zh: 折外预测模仿了基模型在真正新数据上的表现，而这才是元分类器要学会应对的。

title.en: Bagging: more data from the same data
title.zh: 装袋：从同一份数据里变出更多数据

text.en: The intuition: more data means lower variance, but we have only one training set. **Bagging** (bootstrap aggregating) makes new training sets from it by **sampling with replacement**.
text.zh: 直觉：数据越多，方差越低，可我们只有一份训练集。**装袋**（bagging，bootstrap aggregating）用**有放回采样**从它造出新的训练集。

items.en: From the $N$ training instances draw $N$ times **with replacement**: a **bootstrap sample**, the same size as the original, with some instances repeated and others missing.
items.zh: 从 $N$ 个训练实例中**有放回**地抽 $N$ 次：得到一份**自助样本**（bootstrap sample），大小和原来一样，有些实例重复出现，有些缺席。

items.en: Do it $k$ times; train one base classifier (the same algorithm) on each sample.
items.zh: 这样做 $k$ 次；在每份样本上训练一个基分类器（同一个算法）。

items.en: Predict by majority vote (classification) or average (regression).
items.zh: 用多数投票（分类）或平均（回归）来预测。

text.en: Example with $N = 10$: from the instances $1, \dots, 10$ one bootstrap sample is $10, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 9, 3, 10, 9$. It holds only 6 distinct instances; $1, 2, 6, 7$ are missing.
When it works
text.zh: 什么时候有效

items.en: The base algorithm must be **unstable** (high variance: small changes in the data change the model a lot), for example a deep decision tree or a $1$-nearest-neighbour classifier. A stable method such as Naive Bayes barely changes between samples, so there is nothing to average away.
items.zh: 基算法必须**不稳定**（方差高：数据小变动，模型大变动），例如深的决策树、1-最近邻。朴素贝叶斯这类稳定方法，在不同样本间几乎不变，没有什么可平均掉的。

items.en: Simple (sampling and voting), **parallelisable** (the members are independent), and highly effective on **noisy** data: an outlier is missing from about a third of the samples and its influence is diluted.
items.zh: 简单（采样加投票）、可以**并行**（成员互相独立），在**有噪声**的数据上很有效：一个离群点会缺席约三分之一的样本，影响被冲淡。

items.en: Generally much better than a single base classifier, and only occasionally substantially worse.
items.zh: 通常明显好于单个基分类器，只是偶尔会明显更差。

summary.en: Out-of-bag error: a free test set
summary.zh: 袋外误差：免费的测试集

text.en: Each bootstrap sample leaves out about 37% of the instances (derived next). Predict every training instance using **only the trees whose samples did not contain it** and compare with its label: the **out-of-bag (OOB) error**. It is an honest error estimate that needs no separate validation set.
text.zh: 每份自助样本都会漏掉约 37% 的实例（下面推导）。对每个训练实例，**只用样本中不含它的那些树**来预测，再和标签比较，得到**袋外（OOB）误差**。这是一个诚实的误差估计，不需要另留验证集。

title.en: How much of the data does a bootstrap sample contain?
title.zh: 一份自助样本含多少数据？

say.en: $q_1$ is the chance that instance $j$ is missed by one draw. Each draw picks one of the $N$ instances uniformly, so a given instance is **not** picked with probability $1 - 1/N$.
say.zh: $q_1$ 是实例 $j$ 在一次抽取中被漏掉的概率。每次抽取从 $N$ 个实例中均匀地选一个，所以某个实例**没**被选中的概率是 $1 - 1/N$。

say.en: $q_N$ is the chance of being missed by all $N$ draws. The draws are independent (sampling with replacement), so the probabilities multiply.
say.zh: $q_N$ 是 $N$ 次抽取全都漏掉它的概率。各次抽取相互独立（有放回），所以概率相乘。

say.en: Take the logarithm to turn the power into a product.
say.zh: 取对数，把幂变成乘积。

say.en: For small $x$, $\ln(1-x) \approx -x$ (Taylor series). Put $x = 1/N$ and multiply by $N$: the leading term is exactly $-1$, the rest shrinks as $N$ grows.
say.zh: $x$ 小时 $\ln(1-x) \approx -x$（泰勒展开）。令 $x = 1/N$ 再乘 $N$：首项恰好是 $-1$，其余项随 $N$ 变大而消失。

say.en: Exponentiate back. The chance that an instance is **left out** tends to $1/e \approx 0.368$.
say.zh: 再取指数。一个实例**被漏掉**的概率趋于 $1/e \approx 0.368$。

say.en: So a bootstrap sample contains about **63.2%** of the distinct training instances.
say.zh: 所以一份自助样本约含**63.2%** 的不同训练实例。

say.en: The limit is reached quickly: already at $N = 10$ it is 0.65.
say.zh: 极限很快就到了：$N = 10$ 时已经是 0.65。

intro.en: The lecture's bootstrap example shows repeats and missing instances. How many instances are missing, on average, for large $N$?
intro.zh: 课上的自助采样例子里有重复的，也有缺席的实例。$N$ 很大时，平均缺席多少？

outro.en: Each tree trains on roughly 63% of the data and is tested (out of bag) on the other 37%. Because the 63% overlaps a lot between samples, the trees are correlated: the next derivation shows why that limits what averaging can do.
outro.zh: 每棵树大约用 63% 的数据训练，用另外 37% 来（袋外）测试。不同样本之间这 63% 重叠很多，所以树之间是相关的：下一个推导会说明这怎样限制了平均的效果。

title.en: Random forests: decorrelate the trees
title.zh: 随机森林：让树互不相像

text.en: A **random tree** is a decision tree where, at each node, only a random subset of the attributes is considered (a fixed proportion, or about $\sqrt F$ of the $F$ features, a common default; Breiman 2001). It is faster to build than a normal tree, and as a single model it has **higher variance**. This is **feature manipulation**.
text.zh: **随机树**是这样一棵决策树：在每个节点，只考虑随机抽取的一部分属性（一个固定比例，或者 $F$ 个特征里约 $\sqrt F$ 个，这是常见的默认值；Breiman 2001）。它比普通树建得快，作为单个模型**方差更高**。这是**特征操纵**。

text.en: A **random forest** is an ensemble of random trees combined by voting, each trained on its own **bootstrap sample** (instance manipulation). Two sources of randomness, one purpose: to minimise the ensemble's variance without adding bias.
text.zh: **随机森林**是用投票组合起来的一批随机树，每棵树各用自己的**自助样本**训练（实例操纵）。两重随机性，一个目的：在不增加偏差的前提下，把集成的方差压到最低。

rows.en: Generally a very strong performer; robust to overfitting (more trees do not overfit)
rows.zh: 通常表现很强；抗过拟合（树越多不会过拟合）
牺牲了可解释性（几百棵树）
可并行，出乎意料地高效

rows.en: Each single random tree has higher variance than a normal tree
rows.zh: 单棵随机树的方差比普通树高

prompt.en: In a random forest, why is each split chosen from a random subset of the features?
prompt.zh: 随机森林里，为什么每次分裂只从随机抽取的一部分特征里选？

label.en: To make each tree more accurate on its own
label.zh: 让每棵树自身更准

feedback.en: It does the opposite: a single random tree is usually a bit **worse** than a normal tree.
feedback.zh: 恰恰相反：单棵随机树通常比普通树略**差**。

label.en: To make the trees different from each other, so averaging them removes more variance
label.zh: 让树彼此不同，这样平均能消除更多方差

label.en: To remove the bias of the trees
label.zh: 消除树的偏差

feedback.en: Averaging does not change the bias of its members; the lever here is variance.
feedback.zh: 平均不会改变成员的偏差；这里起作用的杠杆是方差。

explain.en: If one feature is very strong, every bootstrap tree splits on it first and the trees look alike (high correlation $\rho$). Hiding it from some splits decorrelates them. The next derivation shows how much $\rho$ matters.
explain.zh: 如果有一个特征特别强，每棵自助树都会先拿它分裂，树就长得很像（相关性 $\rho$ 高）。在一些分裂里把它藏起来，树就不那么像了。下一个推导会说明 $\rho$ 有多重要。

title.en: Why averaging reduces variance
title.zh: 为什么平均能降低方差

say.en: The ensemble's prediction is the average of the $M$ members' predictions at a point $x$ (for classification, think of the predicted score).
say.zh: 集成的预测是 $M$ 个成员在点 $x$ 处预测的平均（分类时，把预测的得分当作这个量）。

say.en: A constant factor comes out of a variance **squared**: $\mathrm{Var}(cX) = c^2\mathrm{Var}(X)$, here $c = 1/M$.
say.zh: 常数因子从方差里提出来要**平方**：$\mathrm{Var}(cX) = c^2\mathrm{Var}(X)$，这里 $c = 1/M$。

say.en: The variance of a sum is the sum of the variances **plus every pairwise covariance**. If the members were independent the covariances would vanish.
say.zh: 和的方差等于各方差之和**再加上每一对的协方差**。如果成员相互独立，协方差就消失了。

say.en: Assume each member has variance $\sigma^2$ (over the randomness of the training sample) and each pair has correlation $\rho$, so covariance $\rho\sigma^2$.
say.zh: 假设每个成员的方差为 $\sigma^2$（针对训练样本的随机性），每一对的相关系数为 $\rho$，协方差就是 $\rho\sigma^2$。

say.en: Count the ordered pairs with $i \neq j$: $M$ choices of $i$, then $M-1$ of $j$.
say.zh: 数 $i \neq j$ 的有序对：$i$ 有 $M$ 种选法，$j$ 再有 $M-1$ 种。

say.en: $M$ variance terms and $M(M-1)$ covariance terms.
say.zh: $M$ 个方差项，$M(M-1)$ 个协方差项。

say.en: Divide through by $M^2$.
say.zh: 整体除以 $M^2$。

say.en: Use $\frac{M-1}{M} = 1 - \frac1M$: $\rho\sigma^2 - \frac{\rho\sigma^2}{M} + \frac{\sigma^2}{M}$, then collect the $\frac1M$ terms.
say.zh: 用 $\frac{M-1}{M} = 1 - \frac1M$：得 $\rho\sigma^2 - \frac{\rho\sigma^2}{M} + \frac{\sigma^2}{M}$，再把含 $\frac1M$ 的项合并。

why.en: Check the extremes: $\rho = 0$ gives $\sigma^2/M$; $\rho = 1$ gives $\sigma^2$ for every $M$.
why.zh: 验证两个极端：$\rho = 0$ 得 $\sigma^2/M$；$\rho = 1$ 时无论 $M$ 多大都是 $\sigma^2$。

intro.en: Take $M$ models whose predictions at a point have the same variance $\sigma^2$ and are pairwise correlated with coefficient $\rho$. What is the variance of their average?
intro.zh: 取 $M$ 个模型，它们在某点的预测方差都是 $\sigma^2$，两两相关系数是 $\rho$。它们的平均的方差是多少？

outro.en: A term that shrinks with $M$, $\frac{1-\rho}{M}\sigma^2$, and a **floor** that more members cannot touch, $\rho\sigma^2$.
outro.zh: 一项随 $M$ 变小：$\frac{1-\rho}{M}\sigma^2$；另一项是更多成员也动不了的**下限**：$\rho\sigma^2$。

prompt.en: How many ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $i \neq j$ are there among $M$ members?
prompt.zh: $M$ 个成员里，$i \neq j$ 的有序对 $(i,j)$ 有多少个？

title.en: What the formula says
title.zh: 这个公式在说什么

alt.en: Variance of the average against the number of members M for correlations 0, 0.3, 0.6 and 1. Each curve falls and flattens at a floor equal to its correlation; correlation 1 does not fall at all.
alt.zh: 成员数 M 增加时，平均的方差随之变化，相关系数分别为 0、0.3、0.6、1。每条曲线下降后在等于相关系数的水平处走平；相关系数为 1 的完全不降。

items.en: **Independent members** ($\rho = 0$): variance $\sigma^2/M$; add members and it vanishes.
items.zh: **成员独立**（$\rho = 0$）：方差 $\sigma^2/M$，加成员它就消失。

items.en: **Correlated members:** the variance stops at $\rho\sigma^2$. With $\rho = 0.3$, a hundred trees give only a 3x reduction. **Decorrelating** the members matters more than adding more of them. This is why random forests hide features at each split, and why bagging gains less than the independent curve promised.
items.zh: **成员相关：** 方差停在 $\rho\sigma^2$。$\rho = 0.3$ 时，一百棵树也只降到约三分之一。**降低相关性**比再加成员更重要。这正是随机森林在每次分裂时藏起一些特征的原因，也是装袋的收益达不到独立曲线所许诺的原因。

items.en: **Bias is untouched:** $E[\bar f] = E[f_i]$ when members share the same expectation. Averaging cuts variance only, so it helps low-bias, high-variance members (deep trees) and does nothing for high-bias ones (shallow stumps). That is the job of boosting.
items.zh: **偏差不变：** 成员期望相同时 $E[\bar f] = E[f_i]$。平均只降方差，所以对低偏差、高方差的成员（深树）有帮助，对高偏差的成员（浅的树桩）没有用。那是提升的任务。

prompt.en: Members have $\rho = 0.3$ and $\sigma^2 = 1$. What does the variance of the average approach as $M$ grows?
prompt.zh: 成员的 $\rho = 0.3$，$\sigma^2 = 1$。$M$ 变大时，平均的方差趋近于多少？

feedback.en: That needs $\rho = 0$. With positive correlation there is a floor.
feedback.zh: 那要 $\rho = 0$ 才行。相关性为正时存在下限。

feedback.en: $0.7 = 1 - \rho$ is the part that **does** vanish, $\frac{1-\rho}{M}\sigma^2$. The floor is $\rho\sigma^2 = 0.3$.
feedback.zh: $0.7 = 1 - \rho$ 是**会**消失的那部分，即 $\frac{1-\rho}{M}\sigma^2$。下限是 $\rho\sigma^2 = 0.3$。

title.en: Boosting: focus on what is still wrong
title.zh: 提升：盯住还没学会的部分

text.en: Bagging trains members independently and averages away their variance. **Boosting** works differently: members are trained **one after another**, and each one concentrates on the instances the previous ones got wrong. It reduces **bias**, and combines weak members (like one-split decision trees, **stumps**) into a strong one.
text.zh: 装袋让成员相互独立地训练，靠平均抹掉方差。**提升**（boosting）完全不同：成员**一个接一个**地训练，每一个都专注于前面成员判错的实例。它降低的是**偏差**，能把弱的成员（比如只分裂一次的决策树，**树桩**）合成一个强的。

items.en: Start with every instance weighted equally, $w_j = 1/N$.
items.zh: 开始时每个实例权重相等，$w_j = 1/N$。

items.en: Repeat for $T$ rounds: train a classifier $C_i$ with the current instance weights (or on a sample drawn according to them); measure its weighted error; **raise the weights of misclassified instances and lower the others**.
items.zh: 重复 $T$ 轮：用当前的实例权重（或按权重抽出的样本）训练一个分类器 $C_i$；度量它的加权错误率；**把判错实例的权重调高，其余的调低**。

items.en: Combine all the classifiers by **weighted** voting: a better classifier gets a bigger vote.
items.zh: 用**加权**投票组合所有分类器：越好的分类器票越重。

text.en: AdaBoost (adaptive boosting)
text.zh: AdaBoost（自适应提升）

text.en: Labels $y \in \{-1, +1\}$, base classifiers $C_i$ (stumps), instance weights $w_j$ that sum to 1. In round $i$:
text.zh: 标签 $y \in \{-1, +1\}$，基分类器 $C_i$（树桩），实例权重 $w_j$ 之和为 1。第 $i$ 轮：

items.en: $\epsilon_i$: the **weighted error**, the total weight of the instances $C_i$ gets wrong ($\delta = 1$ when the condition holds, else 0).
items.zh: $\epsilon_i$：**加权错误率**，即 $C_i$ 判错的实例的权重之和（条件成立时 $\delta = 1$，否则为 0）。

items.en: $\alpha_i$: the classifier's **vote**, half the log-odds of being right.
items.zh: $\alpha_i$：这个分类器的**票重**，即答对的对数几率的一半。

items.en: $Z_i$: the normaliser that makes the new weights sum to 1.
items.zh: $Z_i$：归一化常数，让新权重之和为 1。

items.en: $C^*$: the final weighted vote (for two classes, the sign of the weighted sum).
items.zh: $C^*$：最终的加权投票（两类时，加权和的符号）。

text.en: In words: a **misclassified** instance has $y\,C = -1$, so its weight is multiplied by $e^{\alpha_i} > 1$; a correct one by $e^{-\alpha_i} < 1$. The lecture states this direction (misclassified up, correct down); the exact factor is derived below.
text.zh: 换成话说：**判错**的实例 $y\,C = -1$，权重乘 $e^{\alpha_i} > 1$；判对的乘 $e^{-\alpha_i} < 1$。课件讲的是这个方向（错的调高、对的调低）；精确的系数在后面推导。

rows.en: almost perfect: a very loud vote
worse than chance: negative vote (flip it)
rows.zh: 比随机还差：负票（反着用）

items.en: **We only trust classifiers that beat random guessing** ($\epsilon < 0.5$ so $\alpha > 0$). As long as every base classifier does, the training error is guaranteed to fall (bound derived below).
items.zh: **我们只信任好于随机猜测的分类器**（$\epsilon < 0.5$，所以 $\alpha > 0$）。只要每个基分类器都做到，训练误差就一定下降（界在后面推导）。

items.en: Boosting is mathematically more complicated but computationally cheap; sequential, so more expensive than bagging. The training error falls fast, and the test error can keep falling after the training error reaches 0. In practice boosting tends to overfit, especially with noisy labels.
items.zh: 提升数学上更复杂，但计算便宜；因为是串行的，比装袋贵。训练误差下降很快，训练误差到 0 之后测试误差还可能继续下降。实际中提升容易过拟合，尤其是标签有噪声时。

title.en: AdaBoost, round 1, fully computed
title.zh: AdaBoost 第 1 轮，完整计算

say.en: Ten instances at $x = 1, \dots, 10$ with labels $+,+,+,-,-,-,-,+,+,+$. No single threshold separates them, so a stump will make mistakes. All weights start equal.
say.zh: 十个实例，$x = 1, \dots, 10$，标签 $+,+,+,-,-,-,-,+,+,+$。没有哪个阈值能把它们分开，所以树桩必然出错。权重一开始都相等。

say.en: The best stump under these weights. It is wrong exactly on $x = 8, 9, 10$ (it predicts $-1$ there).
say.zh: 在这些权重下最好的树桩。它恰好在 $x = 8, 9, 10$ 上出错（那里它预测 $-1$）。

say.en: The weighted error is the total weight of the mistakes.
say.zh: 加权错误率就是错误实例的权重之和。

say.en: The vote of $C_1$: positive, because $0.3 < 0.5$.
The multipliers for the instance weights: $e^{\alpha_1}$ for the three mistakes (up), $e^{-\alpha_1}$ for the seven others (down).
say.zh: 实例权重的乘数：三个错误实例乘 $e^{\alpha_1}$（升），其余七个乘 $e^{-\alpha_1}$（降）。

say.en: The weights after multiplying no longer sum to 1; their total $Z_1$ is the normaliser.
say.zh: 乘完之后权重之和不再是 1；它们的总和 $Z_1$ 就是归一化常数。

say.en: The new weights. The three mistakes went from 0.1 to 0.1667 each, the seven others from 0.1 to 0.0714. Check: $3(0.1667) + 7(0.0714) = 1$.

why.en: The mistakes now hold total weight exactly 0.5: $\frac{\epsilon e^{\alpha}}{Z} = \frac{\epsilon\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)/\epsilon}}{2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}} = \frac12$. So $C_1$ would be at chance on the new weights, and round 2 must find something different.
why.zh: 错误实例的权重之和现在恰好是 0.5：$\frac{\epsilon e^{\alpha}}{Z} = \frac{\epsilon\sqrt{(1-\epsilon)/\epsilon}}{2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}} = \frac12$。所以在新权重下 $C_1$ 恰好和随机一样，第 2 轮必须找出不同的东西。

outro.en: The next two rounds follow the same recipe; the table on the next page has all the numbers.
outro.zh: 接下来两轮照同样的方法；下一页的表里有全部数字。

title.en: Three rounds and the final vote
title.zh: 三轮，以及最后的投票

text.en: Instance weights at the start of each round (round 1 is uniform) and the final score $F(x) = \sum_t \alpha_t C_t(x)$:
text.zh: 每轮开始时的实例权重（第 1 轮是均匀的），以及最终得分 $F(x) = \sum_t \alpha_t C_t(x)$：

items.en: Round 2 puts weight 0.1667 on $x = 8, 9, 10$ and finds the stump that gets them right (but now misses $x = 1, 2, 3$, with $\epsilon_2 = 0.2143$). Round 3 finds a different compromise. Each round's mistakes are other instances.
items.zh: 第 2 轮把 0.1667 的权重压在 $x = 8, 9, 10$ 上，找到能判对它们的树桩（但现在错了 $x = 1, 2, 3$，$\epsilon_2 = 0.2143$）。第 3 轮找出另一种折中。每轮的错误都落在不同的实例上。

items.en: The sign of $F(x)$ is the prediction. It is **correct on all ten instances**, although each stump alone makes 3 or 4 mistakes. Three weak classifiers made a perfect one: Intuition 1, through weights instead of independence.
items.zh: $F(x)$ 的符号就是预测。它在**全部十个实例上都对**，尽管每个树桩单独都错 3 到 4 个。三个弱分类器造出了一个完美的分类器：直觉 1，靠的是权重而不是独立性。

text.en: The lecture's weighted vote
text.zh: 课件里的加权投票

text.en: The vote is $C^*(x) = \arg\max_y \sum_i \alpha_i\,\delta(C_i(x) = y)$: total weight behind $+1$ is $1.0 + 1.5 = 2.5$, behind $-1$ is $3.0$. The answer is **$-1$**, although two of three classifiers say $+1$.
text.zh: 投票 $C^*(x) = \arg\max_y \sum_i \alpha_i\,\delta(C_i(x) = y)$：支持 $+1$ 的总权重是 $1.0 + 1.5 = 2.5$，支持 $-1$ 的是 $3.0$。结果是 **$-1$**，尽管三个里有两个说 $+1$。

prompt.en: $C_2$ has $\alpha_2 = 3.0$. What weighted error does it have?
prompt.zh: $C_2$ 的 $\alpha_2 = 3.0$。它的加权错误率是多少？

label.en: About $0.95$

feedback.en: A large $\alpha$ means a **low** error: $\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$ grows as $\epsilon \to 0$.
feedback.zh: $\alpha$ 大意味着错误率**低**：$\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$ 在 $\epsilon \to 0$ 时变大。

label.en: About $0.5$

feedback.en: At $\epsilon = 0.5$, $\alpha = 0$: no voice at all.
feedback.zh: $\epsilon = 0.5$ 时 $\alpha = 0$：完全没有发言权。

label.en: About $0.0025$: $\epsilon = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\alpha}}$
label.zh: 约 $0.0025$：$\epsilon = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\alpha}}$

explain.en: Invert $\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$: $e^{2\alpha} = \frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$, so $\epsilon = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\alpha}} = \frac{1}{1+e^{6}}$, a nearly perfect classifier, which deserves to outvote the other two together.
explain.zh: 把 $\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$ 反过来：$e^{2\alpha} = \frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$，所以 $\epsilon = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\alpha}} = \frac{1}{1+e^{6}}$，几乎完美的分类器，理应压过另外两个之和。

title.en: Where AdaBoost's vote weights and instance weights come from
title.zh: AdaBoost 的票重与实例权重从哪来

say.en: **Exponential loss** of the score $F$. $y\,F > 0$ means right: the loss is small and shrinks with confidence; $y\,F < 0$ means wrong: the loss is large. It is above the 0-1 error, so shrinking it shrinks the training error.
say.zh: 得分 $F$ 的**指数损失**。$y\,F > 0$ 表示判对：损失小，且越有把握越小；$y\,F < 0$ 表示判错：损失大。它高于 0-1 错误，所以把它压小，训练错误也被压小。

say.en: Build the ensemble greedily, adding one classifier $C_t$ with vote $\alpha$ at a time. The exponential of a sum is a product.
say.zh: 贪心地构造集成，每次加一个分类器 $C_t$，票重为 $\alpha$。和的指数就是指数的积。

say.en: The first factor is already fixed when we add $C_t$. It is **the instance weight**: large for instances the ensemble so far gets wrong or only just right. (At the start $F_0 = 0$, so all weights are equal.) This is where the multiplicative update $w_j \leftarrow w_j e^{-\alpha y C}$ comes from.
say.zh: 加入 $C_t$ 时，第一个因子已经固定。它就是**实例权重**：对目前的集成判错、或只是勉强判对的实例，它很大。（起点 $F_0 = 0$，所有权重相等。）乘法更新 $w_j \leftarrow w_j e^{-\alpha y C}$ 就是由此而来。

say.en: Split the instances. Where $C_t$ is right ($y\,C = +1$, total weight $1-\epsilon$) the factor is $e^{-\alpha}$; where it is wrong (total weight $\epsilon$) it is $e^{\alpha}$.
say.zh: 把实例分成两组。$C_t$ 判对的（$y\,C = +1$，总权重 $1-\epsilon$）因子是 $e^{-\alpha}$；判错的（总权重 $\epsilon$）因子是 $e^{\alpha}$。

say.en: Choose the vote $\alpha$ that minimises the loss: set the derivative to 0.
say.zh: 选使损失最小的票重 $\alpha$：令导数为 0。

say.en: Multiply by $e^{\alpha}$ and rearrange.
say.zh: 两边乘 $e^{\alpha}$ 整理。

say.en: Take the logarithm. This is the lecture's formula: **half the log-odds of being right.** A low error gives a big vote; $\epsilon = 0.5$ gives none.
say.zh: 取对数。这就是课件里的公式：**答对的对数几率的一半。** 错误率低，票重就大；$\epsilon = 0.5$ 就没有。

say.en: Substitute back: $(1-\epsilon)\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}} + \epsilon\sqrt{\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}} = 2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}$. Every round with $\epsilon < \frac12$ shrinks the loss by this factor $Z_t$.
say.zh: 代回去：$(1-\epsilon)\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}} + \epsilon\sqrt{\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}} = 2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}$。每一轮只要 $\epsilon < \frac12$，损失就乘上这个因子 $Z_t$ 而变小。

say.en: $E_{tr}$ is the training error. The per-round factors multiply, and the 0-1 error is below the exponential loss. So **as long as each classifier beats chance, the training error bound falls exponentially in the number of rounds.** In our example the bound is 0.58 after 3 rounds while the real error is already 0: an upper bound, not tight. (Freund and Schapire 1997; the exponential-loss view is due to Friedman, Hastie and Tibshirani 2000.)
say.zh: $E_{tr}$ 是训练误差。各轮的因子相乘，而 0-1 错误低于指数损失。所以**只要每个分类器都好于随机，训练误差的界就随轮数指数下降。** 在我们的例子里，3 轮后界是 0.58，而真实误差已经是 0：这是上界，并不紧。（Freund 与 Schapire 1997；指数损失的观点来自 Friedman、Hastie 与 Tibshirani 2000。）

intro.en: The formulas for $\alpha_i$ and the weight update were just stated. Here is where they come from: AdaBoost greedily minimises the exponential loss. Use labels $y \in \{-1,+1\}$ and members $C_t(x) \in \{-1,+1\}$; the ensemble scores $F(x) = \sum_t \alpha_t C_t(x)$ and predicts $\mathrm{sign}\,F$.
intro.zh: $\alpha_i$ 和权重更新的公式刚才只是给出来的。它们的来源是：AdaBoost 在贪心地最小化指数损失。设标签 $y \in \{-1,+1\}$，成员 $C_t(x) \in \{-1,+1\}$；集成的得分是 $F(x) = \sum_t \alpha_t C_t(x)$，预测 $\mathrm{sign}\,F$。

title.en: Bagging, boosting, stacking side by side
title.zh: 装袋、提升、堆叠对照

rows.zh: 串行，后一个纠正前一个
同一份数据（第 1 层用折外预测）

rows.en: smooths the biases of different algorithms

rows.zh: 视情况；靠折外数据防护
昂贵：很多模型加交叉验证

title.en: Noise
title.zh: 噪声

body.en: A mislabelled instance is always misclassified, so boosting raises its weight round after round and the later classifiers contort themselves to fit it: boosting is sensitive to label noise. Bagging only sees it in some samples, and its vote dilutes the effect: bagging is robust to noise.
body.zh: 一个标错的实例总是被判错，所以提升一轮又一轮地加大它的权重，后面的分类器会扭曲自己去迎合它：提升对标签噪声敏感。装袋只在部分样本里碰到它，投票又把影响冲淡：装袋对噪声稳健。

text.en: General cost of any ensemble: more computation and memory, and less interpretability than one model. Reward: usually higher accuracy and lower variance.
text.zh: 任何集成的共同代价：计算和内存更多，可解释性不如单个模型。回报：通常准确率更高、方差更低。

prompt.en: You have deep, unpruned decision trees (low bias, high variance) on a noisy dataset. Which ensemble fits best?
prompt.zh: 你有深而未剪枝的决策树（低偏差、高方差），数据有噪声。哪种集成最合适？

label.en: Boosting: it fixes the hard instances, which includes the noisy ones
label.zh: 提升：它修正难的实例，包括那些噪声实例

feedback.en: It would chase the noise, and its job (reducing bias) is not what deep trees need.
feedback.zh: 它会去追噪声，而且它的任务（降偏差）并不是深树所需要的。

label.en: Bagging (a random forest): it averages the variance away and dilutes the noise
label.zh: 装袋（随机森林）：把方差平均掉，并冲淡噪声

label.en: Neither: ensembles only help weak classifiers
label.zh: 都不用：集成只对弱分类器有用

feedback.en: Intuition 2: ensembles of strong classifiers are usually at least as good as the best, and bagging is built for exactly such high-variance members.
feedback.zh: 直觉 2：强分类器的集成通常至少不比最好的差，而装袋正是为这类高方差成员设计的。

explain.en: Match the ensemble to the member's weakness: high variance, use bagging; high bias, use boosting.
explain.zh: 根据成员的弱点选集成：方差高用装袋；偏差高用提升。

label.en: Bagging reduces bias, boosting reduces variance
label.zh: 装袋降偏差，提升降方差

feedback.en: Reversed. Averaging independent-ish members cuts variance; boosting fits what is still wrong, cutting bias.
feedback.zh: 弄反了。平均近乎独立的成员降方差；提升拟合还没学会的东西，降偏差。

label.en: Both reduce only variance
label.zh: 两者都只降方差

feedback.en: Boosting's stumps start with high bias; adding them in sequence fits the pattern they individually cannot.
feedback.zh: 提升用的树桩一开始偏差很高；串行地加起来，才拟合了它们单个拟合不了的模式。

label.en: Bagging reduces variance, boosting reduces bias
label.zh: 装袋降方差，提升降偏差

explain.en: Bagging: parallel, simple vote, minimises variance, not prone to overfitting. Boosting: iterative, weighted vote, minimises bias, prone to overfitting.
explain.zh: 装袋：并行、简单投票、压方差、不易过拟合。提升：迭代、加权投票、压偏差、易过拟合。

title.en: Exam practice: majority vote of independent classifiers
title.zh: 考试练习：独立分类器的多数投票

prompt.en: Five independent classifiers each have error rate $0.3$. What is the error rate of their majority vote? Round to 3 decimals.
prompt.zh: 五个相互独立的分类器，错误率都是 $0.3$。它们多数投票的错误率是多少？保留 3 位小数。

hints.en: Wrong means 3, 4 or 5 of the 5 members wrong.
hints.zh: 判错意味着 5 个里有 3、4 或 5 个错。

title.en: Exam practice: the variance of an average
title.zh: 考试练习：平均的方差

prompt.en: Ten models have prediction variance $\sigma^2 = 4$ and pairwise correlation $\rho = 0.25$. What is the variance of their average?
prompt.zh: 十个模型，预测方差 $\sigma^2 = 4$，两两相关系数 $\rho = 0.25$。它们的平均的方差是多少？

title.en: Exam practice: the classifier weight
title.zh: 考试练习：分类器的权重

prompt.en: In an AdaBoost round the weak classifier has weighted error $\epsilon = 0.2$. What is its weight $\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$ (natural log)? Round to 3 decimals.
prompt.zh: AdaBoost 的某一轮里，弱分类器的加权错误率 $\epsilon = 0.2$。它的权重 $\alpha = \frac12\ln\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}$（自然对数）是多少？保留 3 位小数。

title.en: Exam practice: a weight update
title.zh: 考试练习：实例权重更新

prompt.en: Ten instances start with weight $0.1$ each. The first classifier has $\epsilon = 0.3$ (3 instances wrong, $\alpha = 0.4236$). After the update and normalisation, what is the weight of one misclassified instance? Round to 3 decimals.
prompt.zh: 十个实例，权重起初各为 $0.1$。第一个分类器 $\epsilon = 0.3$（错 3 个，$\alpha = 0.4236$）。更新并归一化之后，一个被判错的实例的权重是多少？保留 3 位小数。

explain.en: Unnormalised: $0.1\,e^{0.4236} = 0.1528$. Normaliser $Z = 7(0.0655) + 3(0.1528) = 0.9165$. New weight $0.1528/0.9165 = 0.1667$. (Shortcut: the 3 mistakes now carry half the weight: $0.5/3$.)

hints.en: After normalising, the misclassified instances hold total weight $\frac12$.
hints.zh: 归一化之后，被判错的实例共占权重 $\frac12$。

title.en: Exam practice: stacking validation
title.zh: 考试练习：堆叠的验证

prompt.en: How should the training data of the meta-classifier in stacking be produced?
prompt.zh: 堆叠里元分类器的训练数据应该怎样产生？

label.en: Predict the training instances with the base models trained on all of them
label.zh: 用在全部训练数据上训练的基模型去预测这些训练实例

feedback.en: The base models have seen these instances: their predictions are over-optimistic, and the meta-classifier learns to over-trust the models that overfit.
feedback.zh: 基模型见过这些实例：预测过于乐观，元分类器会学成过度信任那些过拟合的模型。

label.en: Use random labels so the meta-classifier cannot cheat
label.zh: 用随机标签，让元分类器没法作弊

feedback.en: The meta-classifier needs the true labels $y$; cheating is prevented by what the base predictions have seen, not by hiding $y$.
feedback.zh: 元分类器需要真实标签 $y$；防作弊靠的是基模型预测有没有见过这些数据，而不是藏起 $y$。

label.en: With cross-validation: each instance is predicted by base models that were trained without it (out-of-fold predictions)
label.zh: 用交叉验证：每个实例都由没用它训练的基模型来预测（折外预测）

label.en: Average the base models' predictions instead of learning a meta-classifier
label.zh: 不学元分类器，直接把基模型的预测平均

feedback.en: That is plain voting, not stacking.
feedback.zh: 那是普通投票，不是堆叠。

explain.en: Out-of-fold predictions imitate genuinely new data (nested cross-validation).
explain.zh: 折外预测模仿了真正的新数据（嵌套交叉验证）。

title.en: Exam practice: which ensemble for which weakness
title.zh: 考试练习：什么弱点用什么集成

prompt.en: A single decision stump (one split) underfits badly: high bias. Which ensemble method addresses that?
prompt.zh: 单个决策树桩（只分裂一次）严重欠拟合：偏差高。哪种集成方法能解决？

label.en: Bagging stumps trained on bootstrap samples
label.zh: 对树桩做装袋，用自助样本训练

feedback.en: Bagging averages variance. Averaged stumps are still stumps: the bias stays.
feedback.zh: 装袋平均的是方差。平均之后的树桩还是树桩：偏差不变。

label.en: Boosting stumps (AdaBoost)
label.zh: 对树桩做提升（AdaBoost）

label.en: A random forest with a larger feature subset
label.zh: 加大特征子集的随机森林

feedback.en: The feature subset controls the correlation of deep trees; it does not add the capacity that stumps lack.
feedback.zh: 特征子集控制的是深树之间的相关性；它不会补上树桩缺少的容量。

label.en: Simple voting of 100 copies of the same stump
label.zh: 把同一个树桩复制 100 份做简单投票

feedback.en: 100 identical members are one member.
feedback.zh: 100 个相同的成员就是一个成员。

explain.en: Boosting fits what the earlier members got wrong, so a sequence of stumps can represent what no single stump can (see the 10-point example).
explain.zh: 提升拟合前面成员判错的部分，所以一串树桩能表示任何单个树桩表示不了的东西（见那个 10 点的例子）。

title.en: Exam practice: bagging versus boosting (Section A)
title.zh: 考试练习：装袋与提升的比较（A 部分）

prompt.en: Compare bagging and boosting in 3 lines or fewer.
prompt.zh: 用三行以内比较装袋和提升。

key_points.en: bagging: parallel, bootstrap samples, simple vote; reduces variance; not prone to overfitting
key_points.zh: bagging: parallel, bootstrap samples, simple vote; reduces variance; not prone to overfitting

key_points.en: boosting: sequential, reweights instances toward the hard ones, weighted vote; reduces bias
key_points.zh: boosting: sequential, reweights instances toward the hard ones, weighted vote; reduces bias

key_points.en: boosting is prone to overfitting and sensitive to noisy labels; bagging is robust
key_points.zh: boosting is prone to overfitting and sensitive to noisy labels; bagging is robust

model_answer.en: Bagging trains independent classifiers in parallel on bootstrap samples and combines them by simple voting; it reduces variance and is not prone to overfitting. Boosting trains classifiers sequentially, raising the weights of misclassified instances, and combines them by weighted voting; it reduces bias, but is more expensive and prone to overfitting, especially with noisy labels.
model_answer.zh: Bagging trains independent classifiers in parallel on bootstrap samples and combines them by simple voting; it reduces variance and is not prone to overfitting. Boosting trains classifiers sequentially, raising the weights of misclassified instances, and combines them by weighted voting; it reduces bias, but is more expensive and prone to overfitting, especially with noisy labels.

explain.en: A marker looks for: parallel vs sequential, simple vs weighted vote, variance vs bias, and the overfitting/noise difference.
explain.zh: 阅卷看：并行与串行、简单投票与加权投票、方差与偏差，以及过拟合/噪声的差别。

title.en: Exam practice: choose an ensemble (Section C style)
title.zh: 考试练习：选一种集成（C 部分风格）

prompt.en: A hospital wants to predict readmission from 200 noisy features and 5,000 patient records, with about 5% of labels wrong. A single deep decision tree overfits. Propose an ensemble approach, justify it, and say how you would estimate its error. Write about a third of a page.
prompt.zh: 一家医院想用 200 个有噪声的特征和 5000 条病人记录预测再入院，约 5% 的标签有误。单棵深决策树过拟合。提出一种集成方案，说明理由，并说明怎样估计它的误差。写约三分之一页。

key_points.en: bagging / random forest: high-variance trees, averaging reduces variance, bootstrap dilutes noisy labels, parallelisable
key_points.zh: bagging / random forest: high-variance trees, averaging reduces variance, bootstrap dilutes noisy labels, parallelisable

key_points.en: random feature subsets at each split decorrelate the trees (the variance floor is rho sigma^2)
key_points.zh: random feature subsets at each split decorrelate the trees (the variance floor is rho sigma^2)

key_points.en: avoid or be careful with AdaBoost: it increases the weight of mislabelled instances and overfits noise
key_points.zh: avoid or be careful with AdaBoost: it increases the weight of mislabelled instances and overfits noise

key_points.en: estimate error with out-of-bag error or cross-validation on held-out data; stacking with out-of-fold predictions is an option if several model types are available
key_points.zh: estimate error with out-of-bag error or cross-validation on held-out data; stacking with out-of-fold predictions is an option if several model types are available

model_answer.en: I would use a random forest. A deep tree has low bias and high variance, which is exactly what bagging fixes: averaging many trees trained on bootstrap samples lowers the variance, and the 5% wrong labels are diluted because each mislabelled record is absent from about 37% of the samples. Choosing a random subset of features at each split decorrelates the trees, which matters because the variance of the average has a floor of rho*sigma^2. I would avoid AdaBoost, which raises the weight of the mislabelled records every round and would overfit them. The error can be estimated by the out-of-bag error (each record predicted only by trees that did not see it) or by cross-validation. If several different model types performed well, stacking with out-of-fold predictions would be a further option.

explain.en: Match the ensemble to the problem: high-variance members and noise point to bagging / random forest; justify with the variance floor and noise sensitivity; name an honest error estimate.
explain.zh: 让集成方案匹配问题：高方差成员加噪声，指向装袋/随机森林；用方差下限和噪声敏感性来论证；说出诚实的误差估计办法。

title.en: What to remember
title.zh: 要记住的

rows.en: needs diverse, better-than-chance members; independent: error $\sum_{i>n/2}\binom ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{n-i}$
rows.zh: 需要多样、好于随机的成员；独立时错误率 $\sum_{i>n/2}\binom ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{n-i}$
第 1 层从第 0 层的预测里学

rows.en: different models; out-of-fold predictions (nested CV); expensive
rows.zh: 不同的模型；折外预测（嵌套交叉验证）；昂贵

rows.en: 63.2% distinct per sample, 36.8% out-of-bag; unstable base; variance down
rows.zh: 每份样本含 63.2% 不同实例，36.8% 袋外；基模型要不稳定；降方差
装袋 + 每次分裂随机特征

rows.en: decorrelates trees; parallel; strong; not interpretable
rows.zh: 让树去相关；并行；强；不可解释
向错误倾斜地重新加权，加权投票

items.en: Bagging: parallel, simple vote, variance, not prone to overfitting. Boosting: sequential, weighted vote, bias, prone to overfitting.
items.zh: 装袋：并行、简单投票、方差、不易过拟合。提升：串行、加权投票、偏差、易过拟合。

items.en: Correlation sets a floor on what averaging can do: $\rho\sigma^2$. Bias is not reduced by averaging.
items.zh: 相关性给平均能做到的设了下限：$\rho\sigma^2$。平均不会降低偏差。

items.en: Ensemble cost: more computation, less interpretability.
items.zh: 集成的代价：更多计算，可解释性更差。
